specification.objective: Make the authenticated workspace UI feel like one coherent product by reusing existing shared visual components and correcting compact interaction targets while preserving feature-specific workflows.

requirements.statement: Use one responsive, accessible WorkspaceHeader pattern for time clock, settings, employee administration, project administration, and audit pages; descriptions may be omitted without leaving blank layout, and actions wrap without overflow.

Use one shared WorkspaceMetricCard for the equivalent metric tiles in employee administration, project administration, and time clock, with consistent icon, label, value, helper, typography, and surface treatment.
Interactive compact controls in Kanban, backlog, and audit expose at least 48 by 48 logical-pixel hit targets without unnecessarily enlarging icon glyphs or changing actions.
Validate shared components and affected pages for semantic headings, responsive layout, enlarged text, and both light and dark themes.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Shared header and metric components render without overflow at narrow widths and 200% text scaling, and their labels remain available to semantics.
Admin employee, project, time-clock, settings, and audit pages use the shared header; employee and project KPI tiles use WorkspaceMetricCard.
Kanban, backlog, and audit compact interactive targets meet the 48 px minimum in automated widget tests.
All affected widget tests and workspace validation gates pass without changing API, authorization, or persisted behavior.

invariants.statement: Keep the existing brand palette, square-corner visual language, workspace shell, semantic color meanings, and feature-specific table, time-clock, and Kanban layouts.
Keep all existing user-visible labels, data, callbacks, permission checks, loading and error behavior, and route behavior unchanged except for layout semantics and hit-target bounds.
Do not add dependencies or change backend, API, authentication, authorization, or data persistence.

forbidden_states.statement: Equivalent workspace page headers and metric cards continue to use separate duplicated visuals, or compact actions remain below the 48 px accessibility target.
Feature-specific workflows are forced into a generic layout that clips controls or loses their distinct meaning.

inputs.statement: Workspace route, viewport width, text scaling, theme brightness, and control state.

outputs.statement: Consistent shared page headers and metric cards, accessible compact controls, and responsive semantic presentation.

failure_semantics.statement: A widget test fails with a labeled target-size mismatch or layout/semantics assertion when the workspace contract is violated.
